definition.brief: You're the tutor in Study. Help the person learn from their books and the course they're taking: explain the lesson they have open in simple words with a small example, give a hint before an answer, never answer a quiz question for them before they've tried, and say what to study next. For how they're doing, read their own progress.

books: Which book should I start with?
progress: What should I go over again?

lesson_state.formula: =status == "Writing" ? "✍️ Being written" : my_done(mine, lesson) ? "✅ Done" : "✨ New"

book_state.formula: =status == "Reading" && parts > 0.0 && read >= parts ? "✅ Ready" : status == "Reading" ? "📖 Reading: " + string(int(read)) + " of " + string(int(parts)) : status == "Problem" ? "😕 Problem" : "⏳ Waiting for its file"

course_state.formula: =status == "Planning" ? "🧠 Planning the units…" : status == "Writing" ? "✍️ " + of(written_now(to_write, lessons, written), to_write_now(to_write, lessons)) + " lessons written" : status == "Problem" ? "😕 Problem" : "✅ Ready"

right_answer.formula: =answer == "A" ? a : answer == "B" ? b : answer == "C" ? c : d

book_parts.heading: Seeds wake up
book_parts.summary: A seed is a baby plant with a packed lunch. It sleeps in the soil until water soaks in and tells it to start growing.
book_parts.text: Every seed holds a tiny plant and a store of food. It can wait for months. When water soaks through its coat, the seed swells, splits and sends a root down and a shoot up.

book_parts.heading: Good soil
book_parts.summary: Soil holds water, air and food for roots. Worms and crumbs of old leaves make it rich and soft.
book_parts.text: Good soil is crumbly. It holds water like a sponge but lets air in too. Worms mix in old leaves, which become food for the roots.

book_parts.heading: Leaves make food
book_parts.summary: Leaves catch sunlight and use it to turn air and water into sugar, the plant's food. That's photosynthesis.
book_parts.text: A leaf is a little kitchen. It takes in air through tiny holes, water from the roots and light from the sun, and makes sugar. We call this photosynthesis.

study_courses.goal: How plants grow, so I can look after my garden
study_courses.title: 🌱 Plants 101

study_units.title: 🍃 Leaves and light
study_units.about: How a plant makes its own food

study_lessons.title: 💧 Why seeds need water
study_lessons.text:
A seed is like a tiny backpack: inside is a baby plant and a packed lunch to get it started.

It can sleep for months. When water soaks through its coat, the seed swells up, splits open and sends a root down and a shoot up towards the light.

Try it: put a bean on a wet paper towel in a jar. In two or three days you'll see it wake up!

study_lessons.title: 🪱 What good soil does
study_lessons.text:
Good soil is crumbly, like chocolate cake. It holds water like a sponge but still lets air in, and roots need both.

Worms are the soil's helpers: they pull old leaves underground, where they rot into food for the roots.

Squeeze a handful of damp soil. If it crumbles when you poke it, it's just right.

study_lessons.title: ☀️ How leaves make food
study_lessons.text:
A leaf is a little kitchen powered by sunshine. It breathes in air through tiny holes, sips water brought up from the roots and catches light.

With that light it turns air and water into sugar, the plant's food, and lets out the oxygen we breathe. That's photosynthesis.

That's why a plant in a dark cupboard grows pale and weak: its kitchen has no power.

study_questions.why: Water soaking through the coat tells the seed to start growing.

study_questions.question: What does a seed send down first?
study_questions.why: The root goes down first to find water.

study_questions.question: What should good soil feel like?
study_questions.why: Crumbly soil holds water and still lets air in.

study_questions.question: How do worms help the soil?
study_questions.why: The leaves rot into food for the roots.

study_questions.question: What does a leaf make with sunlight?
What does a plant give off that we breathe?
study_questions.why: Leaves let out oxygen as they make food.
